sections.note: These are implementation and interface checks. The optimized candidate has no completed final five-backend physics/runtime campaign. Historical c91 measurements remain separate.
sections.title: Implemented changes and actual installation

claims.scope: 100 saved ordinary physical points; historical policy
claims.text: All five reducers complete the 100-point stream and pass both 3e-6 regression and the 1e-8 target. TIRust accepts 82 points in DP and 18 in QP. This establishes this historical sample only.
claims.title: EW 2→3

claims.scope: 100 saved ordinary physical points; historical policy
claims.text: Baseline/candidate CutTools, Ninja and COLLIER each complete 100 points and pass 3e-6. Ninja and COLLIER miss the 1e-8 target; their worst raw relative residuals against CutTools are 8.26e-7 and 8.30e-7, and they also disagree with each other. CutTools accepts 88 DP/12 QP; Ninja 97 DP/3 QP. Backend 8 has a resource/controller failure despite a saved raw stream; backend 9 times out before READY. Neither failed lane is qualified.
claims.title: QCD 2→4

claims.scope: 100 saved ordinary physical points; historical policy
claims.text: CutTools, Ninja, COLLIER and NinjaRS complete their 100-point observations and pass 3e-6. Ninja, COLLIER and NinjaRS miss the 1e-8 target. CutTools accepts 93 DP/7 QP. TIRust reaches the unchanged 1,800-second startup deadline before completing warmup; partial warmup data are not a complete observation or performance result.
claims.title: EW 2→4

sections.note: These three runs supplement the immutable eight-case pilot index. They use historical generated sources and library bytes, not the pending optimized candidate. Reported DP/QP counts are final accepted outcomes, not internal attempt counts. No timings here qualify performance acceptance.
sections.title: Later historical ordinary-point observations

claims.scope: Frozen original-policy stress and private tensor diagnostics
claims.text: TIRust serves all 200 ordinary-control groups but refuses 37 of 200 threshold groups; automatic code 420 correctly rejects the point. Forced-QP code 120 contains an incomplete sum. An independent pole-ratio identity agrees with NinjaRS to 1.68e-11, while accepted Ninja QP differs by 111 in relative ratio despite its host estimate. Private higher-precision tensor experiments do not establish a repaired full amplitude; the finite coefficient remains unresolved.
claims.title: EW threshold remains unqualified

claims.scope: Original automatic policy versus private unchecked corrections
claims.text: All five reducers pass the 19 moderate points. The two extreme points remain unqualified under the original automatic policy. Private CutTools scalar-cutoff and QP denominator-transport corrections resolve one fixed-QP discrepancy to 2.11e-11 and agree with an independent double-pole formula. Those results remain unchecked diagnostics, with no promoted CutTools change or automatic stability qualification.
claims.title: Complex-mass extremes remain open

claims.text: At original points 39, 60, 91 and 93, the added TIRust trace observes both host failure flags false on all nine public calls, and the final values exactly match the original QP adjudication. An independently pinned reparse covers the earlier parser-provenance omission. The result supports reported completeness for these calls; it does not turn unchecked QP into automatic acceptance.
claims.title: QCD 2→3 QP completeness supplement

claims.scope: Private tracing driver; acceptance executable unchanged
claims.text: The complete 100-point stream is warmed before cohort membership is frozen. Per-call status, absolute NinjaRS retry counters and DP/QP failure flags expose compensated DP, rescue and migrations. The schema-2 n1 run has no flagged calls or migrations, but its seven timed batches last only 0.800–0.809 seconds: the diagnostic median is null. Final-candidate DP/QP cohort measurements are pending; internal algorithm attempts are not reconstructed.
claims.title: Native-DP and rescued cohort protocol

claims.text: The Born-only fallback and host edge fixtures pass their local arithmetic, exception and policy checks. The full soft/collinear physical request still fails checked loop evaluation with code 420. A finite repaired Born term alone does not qualify the virtual amplitude; this prototype remains private.
claims.title: Private Born fallback does not repair stress

sections.note: Independent pole identities, higher precision and native failure flags qualify different questions. An unchecked positive-mode code 120 does not establish that every tensor contributed, and a false failure flag alone does not prove accuracy.
